cards.text: Isaiah the prophet brings a new message from the LORD of Hosts. No small talk, no warm-up. It opens with an OATH: the LORD of Hosts has sworn.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts swears an oath about His plan. True or false: He says His plan might still change.

cards.text: He says, "Surely, as I have planned, so will it be; as I have purposed, so will it stand." Me? I've been "planning" to clean my oven so long the crumbs in there started paying RENT.
Then the LORD names who this plan is about: Assyria, the land where Nineveh stood (Genesis 10:11). An oath and then a name, friend, and I'm leaning in so close my mustache is in the dough.

cards.question: The LORD has sworn His plan will stand. What does He say He will do to Assyria in His land?

cards.text: The LORD keeps going: "I will trample him on My mountain." My land, My mountain, friend, this is the LORD's home turf.
Then the LORD talks about a yoke and a burden. Assyria has put them on somebody's shoulders.

cards.question: Whose shoulders does the LORD say Assyria's yoke and burden will be taken off?

cards.text: Then the message zooms way, WAY out.

cards.question: The message zooms out: this is the plan devised for the whole ___.
True or false: the message pictures the LORD's hand stretched out over all the nations.

cards.text: Then it ends with two questions, and they just hang there: "The LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who can thwart Him? His hand is outstretched, so who can turn it back?"

cards.question: The message asks who can thwart the LORD of Hosts and who can turn His hand back. What answer do those questions expect?

answers.text: Only all the nations together can

cards.question: True or false: the message says a big enough army could turn back the LORD's outstretched hand.

findings.problem: Card 4, the setup before this choice card, only introduces Assyria as the land where Nineveh stood. Nothing so far tells the baker that Assyria is a threat or that it oppresses anyone. The yoke and burden don't come up until card 7. Without that, a baker can't reason why the LORD's sworn plan would break Assyria instead of making a treaty or giving it land, so the pick is mostly luck. Card 4 needs context about Assyria, such as the empire pressing on God's people, that doesn't give away the answer. Or the question could move to after the yoke is told.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank is the next words of a line from Isaiah 14:26 the baker hasn't seen yet ("the plan devised for the whole ___"). That makes it a test of wording, not meaning. Card 9's setup also gives the answer away. Saying the message "zooms way, WAY out" rules out "city" and "kingdom" before the baker reasons anything. Ask about the meaning of the zoom out instead, such as how far the plan reaches compared with Assyria and Israel, with a setup that doesn't eliminate the wrong answers.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup line "Then the message zooms way, WAY out" rules out the wrong answers "city" and "kingdom" on the next card. Both are smaller than or the same size as the Assyria and Israel picture already told.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 14 asks the same thing card 13 just settled: no one can turn back the LORD's hand. The only difference is an army the text never mentions. It adds no new detail from the passage. The docs allow an easy follow-up that builds on an earlier answer, but this one only repeats it.
findings.question: Is a choice card that repeats the answer just given on the card before it, reworded with a made-up detail like an army, an allowed easy follow-up? Or should it be replaced with a question about another detail of the passage?
